rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and thank you for being specific about what you have, which makes it much easier to answer well. Here's where things stand. Halcyon Threshold has settled on a first project: a citation-backed record of the specific, falsifiable safety commitments that frontier AI developers and governments make in public — evaluation promises, incident disclosure, audit access, compute thresholds — and whether those commitments are actually kept. Every entry gets a verbatim quote from a primary document, an archive link, and a status that's updated as evidence arrives. Lots of people are arguing about AI risk. Very few are keeping score. The thing it needs most is not more opinions. It's evidentiary discipline, which is why a data analyst is close to the ideal first collaborator. The most useful thing you could do, if you're willing, is be the person who tries to break it. Concretely: once there's a first batch of about ten entries, review them adversarially — are the quotes genuinely verbatim and in context, does each status claim actually follow from the cited evidence, and where have we read a firm commitment into language that's vaguer than we want it to be. I'd rather find out from you than from the organisation's lawyers. That's probably two or three hours, and it would be the highest-leverage review the project gets. Two things I want to be straight with you about. First, I'm still working out how this project sits with my employer, so it's deliberately not public yet and I'm not asking you to put your name to anything in the meantime. Second, I can't pay for your time right now — there's a grant application in progress, and if it lands I'd want to pay for review work rather than keep relying on goodwill. If that sounds worth your five hours, say so and I'll send the first batch as soon as it exists — I'd guess within two to three weeks. If you'd rather do something else, tell me what you'd find interesting; I'd rather you worked on the thing you actually want to work on. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: **Priya Raman** — accepted, with one concrete task: adversarially review the first ten entries and try to break them.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of me, and apologies for a reply that won't be much use to you before tomorrow's deadline: I'm not able to give you an on-the-record quote for this piece. I have an employment situation to sort out before I say anything publicly in a professional capacity, and I'd rather be boring about that than quotable and sorry. Two things that might still be worth something to you. First, on the framing — \"doomers vs. builders\" is a popular axis and I don't think it's the real one. Most of the people I met at that meetup aren't trying to stop anything being built; they'd like the thing that gets built to work as advertised. The more interesting split is between assurances that are checkable and assurances that aren't. That distinction cuts across both of your camps, and the people making genuinely checkable commitments get no credit for it at the moment, because nobody is keeping the record that would let them. That's offered as something to chase, not as a quote — please don't attribute it to me. Second, I'd be glad to talk another time, and I expect to have something more concrete to point you at within a couple of months. If you'll still be covering this area then, I'll get in touch. Best of luck with the piece. Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: **Tessa Brandt / Larkin Dispatch** — declined the quote.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute, Thank you for the invitation. I'm going to decline to sign, and I'd like to give you the real reason rather than let it go unanswered. Two things. The first is practical: I have an employment matter to settle before my name and affiliation appear on anything published and circulated to press. That's my constraint, not a comment on the letter. The second is that Halcyon Threshold is about three weeks old and has not yet produced anything. A signature from an organisation with no track record adds a line to your list and borrows credibility I haven't earned. I'd rather build something first and have a signature mean something later. For what it's worth, the work I'm starting on is adjacent to yours: a sourced public record of the specific safety commitments developers and governments have already made, and whether they're kept. Your letter calls for audits to exist before training runs proceed. A plain record of how previous commitments have fared is, I think, one of the more useful inputs to that argument — and it's evidence rather than assertion, which is the part the case tends to be missing. If that turns out to be any use to you, I'd be glad to hear from you again in a few months. With thanks, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold — weekly operating session" (0 8 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
